faqs.a:
(a)
It shall be unlawful for any person, by use of force, violence, threat thereof or
               any other means creating a substantial risk of injury, intentionally to prevent or
               attempt to prevent any police officer, acting under color of his official authority,
               from effecting an arrest of the actor or another.
(b)
It is no defense to a prosecution under this section that a police officer was attempting
               to make an arrest which was in fact unlawful if he was acting under color of his official
               authority and in making the arrest he did not resort to such excessive force as to
               give rise to a right of self-defense under state law.
(Code 1960, § 17-18; Code 1981, § 21-15)
State Law reference—
Similar provisions, C.R.S. § 18-8-103.
